results.summary: Every proposition in the section was checked word by word against M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A on malegislature.gov and against 247 CMR 9.18(1) through (10) in the 12/6/24 official publication of 247 CMR 9.00, and each matched. The three duties are kept apart with the correct actor and trigger on each; the two limbs of 247 CMR 9.18(4) are taught as two; the regulatory and statutory content lists are set side by side with the three places the regulation reaches further correctly named (indication, disposal, adverse reaction); the s. 21A declination disclaimer is confined to the section it is stated of, and the section says so without asserting a conclusion for 247 CMR 9.18(4) that the regulation does not state; the off-site pathway is taught as two steps, access and the container label; the presumption is correctly keyed to the absence of a refusal record rather than to an affirmative counseling note; the sign and consultation-area elements match the regulation's dimensions, letter height, placement, wording and access-route conditions; and the two inpatient carve-outs are kept distinct, one keyed to the practitioner and one to the drug, with 42 USC 1396r-8 preserved as the reservation rather than generalised to federal regulation at large. All twelve listed practice questions (MA-Q-0086, 0213, 0281 through 0287, 0372, 0418, 0419) are answerable from the section on their released keys and none is contradicted by it. I found nothing wrong.

results.summary: The s. 21 label list, the accessibility paragraph, the pamphlet paragraph and the labeling-reach paragraph were read verbatim on malegislature.gov; s. 18D and s. 20(a) likewise; 247 CMR 9.04(3), (7) and (8) and 247 CMR 8.01(3), 8.03(4)(c) and 8.04(4)(c) were read in the current official Board publications. Every element, qualifier and closing reservation the section states matched. The label list is stated exactly, with the veterinary 'unless' and the tablet-or-capsule condition correctly identified and the prescriber's registration number correctly excluded. 247 CMR 9.04(3) is taught as a failure-contingent and time-bounded alternative with legibility as the standard rather than the trigger. 247 CMR 9.04(7) is taught as an ordered chain into the computerized pharmacy system, with generic-only distribution as the trigger. The telephone-receipt material is the strongest part: the section refuses to let 247 CMR 9.04(8) settle the act, adds the self-identification condition and the closing 'except where otherwise prohibited by federal or state laws and regulations' reservation from 247 CMR 8.04(4)(c), places the pharmacy technician trainee outside the activity under 247 CMR 8.03(4)(c), qualifies the intern limb with 247 CMR 8.01(3), and points at M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(a) for an oral controlled-substance prescription without overstating a conclusion the texts do not give. The pamphlet and s. 18D duties are kept as two duties with exceptions that do not travel, and the first pamphlet exception keeps its c. 111, s. 227 cross-reference. All nine listed practice questions (MA-Q-0110, 0111, 0374, 0375, 0376, 0380, 0381, 0400, 0430) are answerable from the section on their released keys and none is contradicted. I found nothing wrong.

results.summary: The statute was read on malegislature.gov and both regulations were read in their current official publications. Every element matched. The four core verbs and the three may-include limbs are correctly separated, with the three conditions on the laboratory limb stated together and the diagnostic boundary correctly taught as surviving a properly ordered test. The three-instrument qualification table is accurate element by element, including the point that decides fact patterns: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c) requires five years of experience unless 16.02(1)(c)1. (a doctor of pharmacy degree together with an agreement entered on or before June 30, 2017) or 16.02(1)(c)2. is satisfied, while M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b)(3) and 243 CMR 2.12(2)(c) state the degree as a free-standing alternative; the section's reason for treating the narrower provision as operative for a pharmacist proposing to practise is sound, since 243 CMR 2.12(1) makes meeting 247 CMR 16.02 part of the definition of an authorized pharmacist and both 247 CMR 16.03 and 243 CMR 2.12(4) admit only pharmacists meeting 247 CMR 16.02(1). The per-occurrence, term-long and drug-therapy-specific insurance wording, the absence of a continuing education unit alternative in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(e), the four settings with their separate approving bodies, the ambulatory care clinic's cumulative on-site supervision condition, the shared c. 111, s. 51 licensing provision, the purpose-based employment rules and the community pharmacy label in 247 CMR 16.04(7)(b) and (c), the two independent sentences of 243 CMR 2.12(3)(d) including a restriction of a state or federal controlled substances registration, the discretionary and event-limited notification in 243 CMR 2.12(3)(e), the statutory patient definition with its setting-specific notice and consent and its dual recording duty, and the two meanings of Referral with the community-pharmacy written referral's non-exhaustive contents are all stated correctly. All eleven listed practice questions (MA-Q-0081, 0301 through 0306, 0342, 0343, 0360, 0416) are answerable from the section on their released keys and none is contradicted. I found nothing wrong.
